title: General r×r Lindström-Gessel-Viennot Determinant
description: Generalizes the 2×2 LGV lemma to the full r×r case: the number of r-tuples of pairwise non-intersecting lattice paths equals det[e(Aᵢ,Bⱼ)], the determinant of the path count matrix. Formalizes LGVConfig, PathTuple, permutation path tuples, and the Gessel-Viennot sign-reversing involution infrastructure.

meta.author: Lindström (1973), Gessel-Viennot (1985)

overview.historicalContext: The Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) lemma is one of the most versatile tools in enumerative combinatorics. Bernt Lindström proved a general version for vector matroids in 1973, building on ideas from Karlin and McGregor's 1959 work on coincidence probabilities of Markov chains. Ira Gessel and Gérard Viennot independently rediscovered and popularized the result in their influential 1985 paper, providing the elegant sign-reversing involution proof that has become the standard approach. The lemma connects non-intersecting lattice paths to determinants: the number of $r$-tuples of pairwise non-intersecting paths equals $\det[e(A_i, B_j)]_{i,j}$. This determinantal structure has profound consequences—it underlies the Jacobi-Trudi identity for Schur polynomials, the Cauchy-Binet identity in linear algebra, and the Kasteleyn method for perfect matchings. The GV involution is a paradigmatic example of the 'cancellation via involution' technique that pervades algebraic combinatorics.
overview.problemStatement:
**The r×r LGV Lemma**: Given strictly increasing source points A₁,...,Aᵣ and target points B₁,...,Bᵣ on a lattice grid of width m, the number of r-tuples of pairwise non-intersecting lattice paths (Pᵢ: Aᵢ→Bᵢ) equals

  det[ e(Aᵢ, Bⱼ) ]_{i,j=1}^r

where e(A,B) = C(m + (bⱼ - aᵢ), m) is the number of monotone lattice paths from A to B.
overview.text: Generalizes the 2×2 LGV lemma to the full r×r case: the number of r-tuples of pairwise non-intersecting lattice paths equals det[e(Aᵢ,Bⱼ)], the determinant of the path count matrix. Formalizes LGVConfig, PathTuple, permutation path tuples, and the Gessel-Viennot sign-reversing involution infrastructure.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Gessel-Viennot Involution**:
1. Expand det M = Σ_σ sign(σ) ∏ᵢ M_{i,σ(i)} where M_{i,j} = e(Aᵢ, Bⱼ)
2. Each term ∏ M_{i,σ(i)} counts σ-path tuples (Pᵢ: Aᵢ→B_{σ(i)})
3. For σ ≠ id: find smallest i with σ(i) ≠ i; paths Pᵢ and P_{σ(i)} must cross
4. Swap tails at first crossing point → maps σ-tuple to (swap(i,σ(i))∘σ)-tuple
5. sign changes (transposition): terms cancel pairwise
6. Only σ = id survives; non-NI id-tuples also cancel → niTupleCount = det M
keyInsights: The sign-reversing involution pairs each σ-tuple with a τ-tuple where τ = swap(i,σ(i))∘σ has opposite sign, causing pairwise cancellation
Strict monotonicity of sources is essential: if i < σ(i), then aᵢ < a_{σ(i)}, forcing the path from lower source to higher target to cross the path from higher source
The 2×2 case is the base case; the r×r generalization uses the SAME involution mechanism but on r-tuples indexed by Equiv.Perm (Fin r)
pathMatrix determinant non-negativity follows immediately from the LGV lemma since niTupleCount is a natural number
The LGV lemma connects combinatorics to linear algebra: non-intersecting lattice paths encode determinantal identities
The sole remaining axiom (gv_involution_cancellation) isolates the hardest part: showing the involution is well-defined, is its own inverse, and has exactly the NI identity tuples as fixed points

sections.title: Part 1: Lattice Path Foundations
sections.summary: LPath (List Bool), PathMN subtype with Fintype instance (via Vector equivalence), pathCount as binomial coefficient.

sections.title: Part 2: Column Entry and Non-Intersection
sections.summary: northBeforeEast (recursive y-tracking), colEntry, colYRange, and NonIntersecting predicate via column-disjointness.

sections.title: Part 3: r-Tuple Infrastructure
sections.summary: LGVConfig structure (sources/targets strictly monotone), PathTuple (dependent r-tuple), IsNonIntersecting (pairwise non-intersection).

sections.title: Part 4: Path Weight Matrix
sections.summary: pathMatrix: r×r integer matrix M_{i,j} = C(m+(b_j-a_i), m) counting paths from source i to target j.

sections.title: Part 5: Permutation Path Tuples
sections.summary: PermPathTuple (σ-indexed path tuples), signedPermCount (sign(σ) × product of binomial coefficients).

sections.title: Part 6: Non-Intersecting Tuple Count
sections.summary: niTupleCount: cardinality of non-intersecting identity path tuples, the left-hand side of the LGV lemma.

sections.title: Part 7: Gessel-Viennot Involution Infrastructure
sections.summary: swapTailsAt operation with length preservation, transposition sign theorem, firstNonFixed (smallest non-fixed point with minimality and upward-mapping proofs).

sections.title: Parts 7b–7c: PathMN Cardinality and Algebraic Bridge
sections.summary: pathMN_card (PROVED: C(m+n,m) via double induction + Pascal's rule + cons decomposition), permPathTuple_card (product factorization), det_pathMatrix_eq_signed_sum (det = Σ sign(σ)·|PermPathTuple(σ)|).

sections.title: Part 8: The r×r LGV Lemma
sections.summary: gv_involution_cancellation (axiom: signed sum = NI count) and lgv_lemma_rxr (theorem: niTupleCount = det pathMatrix, proved in 2 lines from algebraic bridge + GV cancellation).

sections.title: Parts 9–10: Corollaries and Applications
sections.summary: Non-negativity of det, r=1 vacuous NI, and lgv_universality. Applications survey: Schur polynomials (Jacobi-Trudi), Catalan numbers, Aztec diamond tilings, plane partitions.

conclusion.summary: Comprehensive formalization of the general r×r LGV lemma infrastructure. Defines the path tuple structures, weight matrix, and non-intersection predicate for arbitrary r. Proves the key sign-change lemma (transposition reverses permutation sign) and establishes non-negativity of the path matrix determinant. The main LGV equality is axiomatized pending the full Gessel-Viennot involution proof.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Applications of the r×r LGV lemma:**
1. **Schur polynomials**: Via Jacobi-Trudi, s_λ = det[h_{λᵢ-i+j}] counts NI lattice paths (semistandard Young tableaux)
**2. Plane partitions**: MacMahon's box formula via LGV on 3D lattice
3. **Aztec diamond**: 2^{n(n+1)/2} tilings via NI path determinant
4. **Random matrices**: Eigenvalue spacing via NI random walk paths.

crossReferences.description: Extends the 2×2 LGV lemma to the full r×r case using permutations and Matrix.det
The ballot problem's reflection principle is the 1D precursor to the LGV lemma's crossing argument
The path matrix entries C(m+bⱼ-aᵢ, m) are binomial coefficients counting lattice paths between grid points

The continuous-time ballot problem via Brownian motion provides the probabilistic counterpart to the general LGV determinant: where this file computes determinants of path-count matrices for r non-crossing discrete paths, the Brownian motion approach computes analogous crossing probabilities in continuous time using the Karlin-McGregor theorem
